pr.title: gh-126024: fix UBSan failure in `unicodeobject.c:find_first_nonascii`
pr.body:
Not sure we can do anything except wrapping the call in a function. Adding an allow list may seem too hard since the line would change everytime we change the code. Or we can just forget about the optimized unaligned load.

* Issue: gh-126024

review_comments.body:
The standard compliant way of loading unaligned memory is to use `memcpy`. If you give `memcpy` a fixed size, then on the platforms which support non-aligned loads (including x86, arm64), you just get a normal load operation:

https://gcc.godbolt.org/z/4fG7h3349

We should use memcpy regardless of the architecture. It doesn't impose any alignment requirements on it's arguments. In other words:

* Get rid of the `#if defined(_M_AMD64) || ...`
* Don't use `load_unaligned`

`memcpy` will generate the correct code even on architectures that do not support unaligned loads: https://gcc.godbolt.org/z/MP7MrKd3b.
Is this what you had in mind?
